result:
Hardening round complete, within the exclusive `maintenance.go` / `maintenance_test.go` / `recovery-work.md` scope. Every review finding is addressed.

## Fixes applied

- **Manifest TOCTOU closed** — `VerifyBackup`/`Restore` now hash the tree against the **single** validated snapshot from `readValidatedManifest`; the old second, unvalidated `m.VerifyBackup` re-read is gone.
- **Hostile manifest input** — bounded manifest bytes (64 MiB) and entry count; per-component name validation (no `..`/`.`, no `:` for drive/NTFS-ADS, no backslash, no trailing dot/space, no control chars, no reserved device names), non-negative bounded sizes, 64-hex digest shape, exact **and portable case-fold** duplicate rejection, and `man.ID == id`.
- **Symlink/reparse refusal** — `maintNoFollow` Lstats every path component under the trusted project root before reading the manifest and each backup file; a hostile-symlink test proves it (skips where Windows denies symlink creation).
- **Streaming under context + size bound** — bounded manifest read; every verify/copy/hash streams through a 1 MiB buffer, checks `ctx.Err()` each iteration, and refuses more than the manifest size. No whole-file `os.ReadFile` of large objects/index.
- **Lease guard before AND after** — `TakeBackup` re-confirms after the copy; a mid-copy lease loss fails the call (no success claim) and **preserves** the artifact.
- **Read-only reader proof** — `proveReader` uses `OpenReadOnly` (changes no staged byte); the staged tree is re-hashed **again** after the proof, before publishing.
- **Publish exclusivity** — `maintPublish` holds an `O_EXCL` lock, refuses an existing destination, then a single rename.

## Escalated to main (portable-primitive difficulty)
Atomic no-clobber **directory** publish is not achievable in pure-Go stdlib: Windows `MoveFile` is no-clobber, but POSIX `rename(2)` replaces an empty target directory and Go exposes no `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`. `maintPublish` gives lock-based exclusion + refuse + single rename — **not** an absolute never-overwrite; `RestoreProof.Note` and comments say so. Main should pick the OS primitive (`MoveFileEx` / `renameat2` via `x/sys`) at the CLI layer, or accept the lock exclusion.

## Interface preserved
Discovered main already wired `internal/cli/backup.go`. My initial ctx-adding change to `VerifyBackup` broke its build, so I reverted `VerifyBackup(id string)` to ctx-free (runs `verifyTree` under a background context; a cancellable variant is available to wire). `TakeBackup(ctx,id)`, `Restore(ctx,id,dest)`, `NewMaintenance`, `MaintenanceOptions`, and `RestoreProof` are unchanged.

## Verification
```
GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -run TestMaintenance -count=1 -v ./internal/store  → 10 PASS, 1 SKIP (symlink needs Windows privilege)
gofmt -l …                → clean
go vet ./internal/store   → clean
go build ./internal/cli   → clean (main's backup.go compiles against the seam)
```
Initial-round work and its one build failure are preserved in `recovery-work.md` §2; the hardening round is recorded in §5 with the escalation and the interface note.
